title: Join physical sparse halo transport with source-bound Gaussian recovery (no new κ)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope
Compose three verified modules: a sparse first-face tape transaction, a shrinking-reference halo evaluator, and a source-bound stream/return codec. Original boundary inputs are copied before core mutation, converted and returned exactly once. Real `Reference(61,3,2,1,8,32)` tests holes and period wrap; 52 saved inputs yield 20 targets. This is the missing physical transport-to-consumer interface, not a new Gaussian lemma. No new κ.

## Sources and verification
Canonical base `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a`; component commits `a2f3ce7358e8103f6eccd404e594276e9ccc04d8` and `630c9c2a5d6373ca103c55108bb606b4868bc6fd`, with Git/SHA256 pins in the joined SOURCES.json. Run `python3 -B research/first-face-reference-join/replay_all.py`, expected `PASS_COMPLETE_FIRST_FACE_HALO_PACKAGE`. Registered normal/optimized, independent whole-period and two-axis unequal-radius checks passed. Mutations reject absent wraps, bad keys, payload changes and missing copies.

## Limits and credit
The fixture uses a core test double; a same-reference fast core, global source/stock, outer routing and all five framework assumptions remain unresolved. @CubeJerry with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance and independent AI review. Credit #4100, #4870, #4205, #4217, #4517, #5081, #6880 and their authors. Apache-2.0.
